sections.kicker: Prepared for THAWR by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: THAWR has a mood. The front door does not say what the brand makes.
sections.keep: The black and white film. A dark brick room and one figure in a heavy tee is a world of its own.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.area: A silent black and white film of a brick room, one man in a black tee at the right edge
pins.what: The hero is a moody film with no words on it.
pins.why: It sets a tone, but a visitor cannot tell if THAWR is workwear, streetwear or a label for something else.
pins.how: Add one line to the film that says what THAWR is and for whom.
pins.label: Your hero
pins.cost: Visitors enjoy the mood and cannot repeat what THAWR sells.

pins.what: The menu is Shop, Collections, Brand, Support.
pins.why: This is how every clothing site names its menu. It says nothing about THAWR's point of view.
pins.how: Name the collections after what they stand for, not what they are.
pins.label: Your menu
pins.cost: The words people read first could belong to any other label in Australia.

pins.area: A tall narrow condensed wordmark, THAWR, in white on black
pins.what: The logo is a tight condensed wordmark that suits the film.
pins.why: It matches the mood exactly and is the only branded element on the front door.
pins.how: Use it as the system: same weight and tone on every surface.
pins.label: Your logo
pins.cost: The sharpest asset THAWR has is used once and then left alone.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at THAWR. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out, and all three point the same way.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on THAWR's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Acne Studios, from another category. A few clear signals tell you the world you are in before you read a word.
